notes: Torah #121 of LM2 (reference 1121) has zero edges of any type in the dataset. The source text is a teaching of encouragement for those who struggle with prayer. Rebbe Nachman consoles his followers who find prayer extremely difficult, using the analogy of a convert who rejoices at merely knowing the words up to 'Baruch She'amar.' He advises breaking prayer into small portions and focusing kavanna on each small section sequentially, rather than being overwhelmed by the whole. The text uses 'בְּחִינָתוֹ' (line 5) in the sense of 'according to one's level' (referencing the Zoharic concept of marei d'yada'in and marei d'ragla'in), not as a structural bechina identity declaration.
